columns.name: localeChosenAt
columns.note:
When a human last CHOSE this locale — see Teacher.localeChosenAt for why
this is separate from `locale` itself.

columns.name: readingScale
columns.note:
Reading preferences (D-140). Persisted on the person rather than in
localStorage for two reasons: they must apply on the FIRST paint, before
any client script runs, or the page reflows under the reader; and they
must follow her between her laptop and her phone. Same treatment as
`locale`, which has the same two constraints.

`readingScale` is a multiplier on the root font size, not a pixel value —
the browser's own font-size setting is the more effective control and this
composes with it rather than overriding it.

columns.name: readingSpacing
columns.note:
0 normal, 1 wide, 2 widest. Opened letter and word spacing has better
support in the reading literature than any font substitution.

columns.name: readingTint
columns.note:
A warm tint over the page. Helps some readers with visual stress and is
reported as unhelpful by others, which is exactly why it is a choice.

columns.name: localeChosenAt
columns.note:
When a human last CHOSE this locale, as opposed to it being detected for
them. Null means "nobody has picked" — the value in `locale` came from
signup provisioning (Accept-Language) or a client mirroring its device.

It exists because `locale` was answering two questions at once, and the
automatic writer kept winning: a client that mirrored the DEVICE language
on every session check-in silently reset a teacher who had deliberately
picked Spanish back to English. Same lesson as D-72/D-73 — split the
column rather than guess which writer meant it. Set by a language picker;
never by a background mirror.
